original.target_description: Front versus back vowel brand-name preferences for convertible/knife; original experiments 1a–1c combined.

n.sample_role: Participants in the pooled product-category subgroup; analytic subgroup n not explicitly printed
n.exclusions: No target-specific exclusions established; n not inferred from t degrees of freedom.

replication.target_description: Shrum et al. (2012), front versus back vowels, convertible/knife; Japanese online adult sample

n.sample_role: Participants in product-category subgroups; analytic n for this simple contrast is not explicitly printed
n.exclusions: Whole project excluded 247 participants failing IMC and ACQ. Reported simple-effect denominator df 821 is inconsistent with subgroup counts; no n inferred.

es.quote: Front vowel sounds were preferred over back vowel sounds for convertible and knife (52.56–47.45%; F 1,821 = 4.717, p = 0.030, η 2 p = 0.011).

p.quote: Front vowel sounds were preferred over back vowel sounds for convertible and knife (52.56–47.45%; F 1,821 = 4.717, p = 0.030, η 2 p = 0.011).

reported_success.quote: Thus, we successfully replicated the previous findings

notes: Replication simple-effect dfs are printed as 1,821 despite category-specific sample counts; retained as printed. Original PDF is two-column text. The glyph b in pb.001 denotes less than; p < .001 is one-tailed. Analytic subgroup n is not explicitly printed.
